page.text:
A *quasigroup* is a magma in which the operation can always be uniquely
undone on either side: for any elements $a, b$, each of the linear
equations $a * x = b$ and $y * a = b$ possesses a unique solution $x, y$.
This property abstracts the concept of division without requiring either
associativity or an identity element.

In combinatorial terms, when the carrier set is finite of cardinality
$n$, the multiplication table (Cayley table) of a quasigroup forms a
*Latin square*: every element of the set appears exactly once in each row
and exactly once in each column. A quasigroup possessing an identity
element is called a *loop*; loops preserve the local invertibility of
division while remaining free from the rigid constraint of associativity.
